title: model-specific runtime optimizations: llama/mistral/qwen GQA/MQA tuning, kernel & scheduling improvements
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: We saw model-specific regressions and suboptimal throughput for a subset of open models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen) driven by quirks in rotary embedding handling, KV cache layout, and quantization edge cases. This PR implements targeted runtime changes: (1) GQA/MQA-aware kernel selection and small-tile GEMM fallback to avoid pathological slowdowns on MQA-packed tensors; (2) Llama-specific rotary embedding path that avoids redundant rescaling for long prefix lengths; (3) Mistral attention kernel special-case for grouped heads to reduce memory copies; (4) KV cache layout normalization for Qwen to align stride access with our continuous-batching engine. It also includes scheduler changes: a soft-priority continuous-batching scheduler that prioritizes low-latency interactive requests while preserving throughput for batched workloads, adaptive batch shaping heuristics, and cache-warmup hints for long-running sessions. Motivation: customers reported 2-3x latency variance and 10-30% throughput loss on Dedicated pools when serving these models. These fixes target reproducible microbenchmarks and production traces. Checklist: - [x] Kernel selection path added and unit-tested - [x] GQA/MQA detection + fallback implemented - [x] Scheduler integrated with existing continuous-batching runtime - [x] Linear/bench CRs: added Microbench for Llama/Mistral/Qwen - [x] CI perf gating included - [x] Docs + rollout notes written Summary of changes: Updated runtime/kernel_selector.cc to support quantization-layout heuristics and small-tile GEMM fallback; added model_quirks.{h,cpp} for per-model heuristics (rotary length, head grouping); adjusted kv_cache layout transform in kv_cache_manager.cc with compatibility layer for existing checkpoint formats; added new scheduler soft-priority queue and adaptive batch shaping in scheduler.cc; added Python microbench harnesses under tools/bench and a new perf CI job. Tests & results: unit tests for kernel selection and kv cache normalization added; full regression test suite passed after two CI reruns. Microbench results (avg over 20 runs) included below. Rollout: feature-flagged behind runtime.feature.model_quirks, rollout by default to Dedicated in Canary region for 72h before wide release. Migration: compatibility layer ensures existing saved KV cache blobs are readable; see migration note.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Can you explain why we need small-tile GEMM fallback for MQA? I thought our blocked kernels covered this case.

Ava Chen: In MQA packing the stride/shape can produce trailing tiles smaller than the kernel tile size; falling back to a small-tile GEMM avoids large zero-pad overhead and memory thrash observed on older GPUs.
Priya Singh: Scheduler change looks good but add a metric for priority inversion detection.
Ava Chen: Added runtime metric runtime.scheduler.priority_inversion in this PR and wired it to the perf dashboard.
Liam O'Connor: KV compatibility layer is clever; ensure rolling upgrades won't blow up offline checkpoints.
Ava Chen: Compatibility layer includes format version check and a migration path; added integration tests that validate old-format reads.
Diego Martinez: CI showed an intermittent flaky test on multi-gpu scheduling, looks like a barrier race.
Ava Chen: Fixed a race in scheduler.cc (commit f1c3d44) and re-ran CI; tests passed.
Priya Singh: Approving after perf results are green and docs are added.

Cost-per-token estimate on Dedicated: ~12% lower due to batching + cache improvements
release_notes: Model-specific runtime optimizations: - Add model_quirks runtime for Llama/Mistral/Qwen to handle rotary embedding, grouped-head attention, and KV layout differences. - GQA/MQA-aware kernel selection with small-tile GEMM fallback to avoid pathological slowdowns. - Soft-priority continuous-batching scheduler to improve interactive latency without sacrificing throughput. - KV cache normalization with compatibility layer for existing checkpoints. Rollout: Canary on Dedicated for 72h, gated by perf metrics.
notes: Feature gated behind runtime.feature.model_quirks. Operations: monitor runtime.scheduler.priority_inversion and per-model perf dashboard for the first week after rollout. If regressions observed, revert by disabling the feature flag on the affected pool.
